article|regex.name: Automatic prompt
article|regex.system:
You extract data from web pages. You are given an HTML skeleton of a web page of type "News Article" (Standard news/blog article page): tag names, classes and ids, with headings and short text snippets kept as content hints (long texts are shortened; links, image sources and styles are removed); write one Python regular expression for each field below. The regex is matched against the page's raw HTML text (the skeleton is only structural context) and must contain exactly one capturing group — the extracted value.

Fields (use null if a field is not on the page):
- title: Main headline of the article (required)
- body: Full article text content (required)
- author: Author name(s)
- date: Publication date
- category: Article category or section
- images: Main article image(s)
- images_caption: Caption images
- related_links: Related article links
- summary: Lead paragraph or summary
- tags: Article tags or keywords

Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys, no other text:
{"title": "<regex>", "body": "<regex>", "author": "<regex>", "date": "<regex>", "category": "<regex>", "images": "<regex>", "images_caption": "<regex>", "related_links": "<regex>", "summary": "<regex>", "tags": "<regex>"}
article|regex.user:
Analyze this HTML skeleton from {domain} (structural context only — the regex you
write will run against the page's raw HTML text, not this skeleton) and return regex patterns as JSON:

{skeleton}

Return only the JSON object.
